content.title: About
content.content: Cookie, marshmallow pie, chocolate covered is a soft cookie with a layer of airy marshmallow in the center, all coated in a thick chocolate glaze. The dessert combines a crunchy cookie texture, sweet fluffy marshmallow, and the bittersweet taste of chocolate.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first recipes for this type of cookie appeared in the United States in the 1970s as part of the "soft" dessert trend.
Traditional marshmallow was originally made from the root of the marshmallow plant, but today gelatin or plant‑based alternatives are used.
Chocolate glaze is often a blend of dark and milk chocolate to balance flavor.
Cookies can be round or shaped as mini bars, making them convenient for snacking.
The contrast of textures makes the product popular with both children and adults seeking a multi‑sensory treat.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Chocolate, especially dark chocolate, contains flavonoids that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Quick energy boost
items.content: Carbohydrates from the cookie and marshmallow raise blood sugar rapidly, providing an instant energy lift.

items.title: Contains a modest amount of protein
items.content: Recipes often use egg whites, adding a small amount of protein.

items.title: Mood improvement
items.content: Chocolate stimulates serotonin production, which can improve mood.

items.title: Calcium from dairy ingredients
items.content: Milk chocolate and occasional milk added to the dough supply calcium.

items.title: Gluten and dairy allergies
items.content: The cookie typically contains wheat flour and dairy, which may trigger reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Marshmallow and chocolate make the product very sweet, contributing to tooth decay and blood‑sugar spikes.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Due to sugars, fats, and carbs, a serving can be calorie‑rich, so portion control is advised.

items.title: Possible trans fats
items.content: Some commercial versions use partially hydrogenated oils that contain trans fats, which are harmful to heart health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the cookie as a standalone treat, crumble it over ice cream, use it to garnish cakes, or simply snack on it between meals. Slightly warming it can melt the chocolate glaze and soften the marshmallow for an extra indulgent experience.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place at 59‑72 °F (15‑22 °C). For longer shelf life (over two weeks) keep refrigerated to prevent the chocolate from melting. Avoid direct sunlight, which can cause the glaze to discolor.
